rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a somersault, whether or not the direction or technique is specified.

example.english: They did a somersault on the grass, and we laughed so hard our stomachs hurt.
example.traditional: 佢喺草地上打咗個筋斗，笑到我哋肚都痛。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hai2 cou2 dei6 soeng6 daa2 zo2 go3 gan1 dau2 siu3 dou3 ngo5 dei6 tou5 dou1 tung3

rows.note: Use this when the somersault is specifically an aerial or gymnastics move rather than a generic body flip.

example.english: That gymnast completed a somersault on the mat.
example.traditional: 嗰位體操員喺墊上完成咗一個空翻。
example.jyutping: go2 wai6 tai2 cou1 jyun4 hai2 zin3 soeng6 jyun4 sing4 zo2 jat1 go3 hung1 faan1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese way to say that someone performs a somersault.

example.english: The kids did a somersault on the grass and refused to go home.
example.traditional: 細路仔喺草地上打關斗，玩到唔肯返屋企。
example.jyutping: sai3 lou6 zai2 hai2 cou2 dei2 soeng6 daa2 gwaan1 dau2 waan2 dou3 m4 hang2 faan1 uk1 kei2

rows.note: Use this as an alternative everyday expression for performing a somersault, especially when emphasizing the flipping motion.

example.english: I did a somersault on the soft mat, and everyone immediately applauded.
example.traditional: 我喺張軟墊上翻跟斗，成班人即刻拍手。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 zoeng1 jyun5 zin3 soeng5 faan1 gan1 dau2 sing4 baan1 jan4 zik1 hak1 paak3 sau2

rows.note: Use this colloquial alternative when talking about someone doing a somersault in a playful or informal context.

example.english: They did a somersault in the living room and laughed themselves silly.
example.traditional: 佢哋喺客廳打清秋，笑到碌晒地。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 hai2 haak3 teng1 daa2 cing1 cau1 siu3 dou3 luk1 saai3 dei6
